question: Does the DENR-NCR 2025 Annual Report's 52-entry Pasig River system management list expand the NCR source-named waterway scope, and which entries can safely be treated as named waterbody leads?

sourceAccess.accessMethod: Reviewed the official PDF text extraction in the browser on 2026-11-20, Section C, report pages 203-204. The earlier local direct-PDF request returned HTTP 403; no access restriction was bypassed and no local PDF, image, or list transcription was retained.
sourceLocators: Annual Report 2025, pp. 203-204, Section C, Monitoring of Waterways of the Pasig River System: four management clusters and their printed entry counts.
Annual Report 2025, pp. 237-239, Section 3.2.8: separate 2024 biodiversity-assessment scope and high-level fish narrative, reviewed in the linked prior artifact.

sourceScope.sourceStatement: The report labels the Pasig River system as covering 52 waterways managed in four clusters.

reportedClusterEntryCounts.reportedAdministrativeContext: Manila City, Pasig City, Mandaluyong City, San Juan, and Makati City
Pateros, Taguig City, Marikina City, and Pasig City

sourceScope.interpretation: This is an agency management-scope list. The report assigns administrative context at cluster level, not a city/municipality or barangay to each printed entry, and supplies no source-matched feature geometry in this section.

nameFormScreen.method: Screened the 52 printed labels by their visible name form only. These counts classify strings, not aquatic feature identity; no untyped name was silently expanded to River or Creek.
nameFormScreen.disposition: The three additional labels without an explicit estero/creek/river term and the two area-labeled contexts remain unresolved feature-name contexts.
nameFormScreen.categoryRelationship: The three counts are mutually exclusive and sum to the 52 reported entries.

crosswalk.normalization: Exact label comparison after case and surrounding-whitespace normalization only; no accent stripping, prefix removal, token reordering, locality-based merging, or geometry match was used.
crosswalk.interpretation: Exact text overlap and name similarity are discovery hints, not proof that two labels identify the same channel or waterbody. Candidate variants are left unmerged.

rightsDecision.decision: Keep aggregate source-scope counts and the attributed review in internal research. Do not redistribute the report's page, images, map, or a copied full list without checking applicable permission.

limits: The annual report's 52 is the report's management-entry count, not a verified count of unique ecological waterbodies or complete NCR waterways.
Cluster membership does not establish that every listed name is located in every city/municipality named for its cluster.
A source name, including a River/Creek/Estero suffix, does not establish route geometry, fish habitat, current fish presence, public access, fishing permission, water quality, or safety.
Cross-cluster names and candidate variants may refer to connected or repeated features, but no merge was made.
No fish species list or fish sampling results are provided by this Section C management scope.
nextActions: Crosswalk individual source names and locality contexts to independent official or peer-reviewed records before converting any management entry into a canonical waterbody lead.
Continue looking for the underlying 2024 Pasig biodiversity dataset through publicly accessible, authorized materials; the annual-report narrative remains non-site-resolved.
Continue freshwater, brackish, marine, and wetland source discovery across all 17 NCR administrative units; do not close NCR or Luzon coverage.
